chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj, intending to go out to Al-Ta'if. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should begin with Hajj from Makkah, and I do not love for him that he should go out from it unless he is in Ihram, and he should not exceed Al-Ta'if, for it is near to Makkah.'

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: Umrah al-Tamattu (Umrah performed with the intention of Hajj)
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُهِلُّ: To begin the ritual by reciting the Talbiyah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim leaving Makkah for Al-Taif during Umrah al-Tamattu?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the proximity of Al-Ta'if to Makkah is used as the legal criterion to determine whether a pilgrim performing Tamattu' must maintain their Ihram state when traveling outside the holy city. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the boundary for exiting Ihram is not merely geographical distance but the conceptual extent of the Haram's influence, ensuring the pilgrim remains in a state of consecration until the Hajj rites are fully completed.
